# GAP-059: `AUTHID` — the procedure silently disappears entirely

Oracle feature: `AUTHID CURRENT_USER` / `AUTHID DEFINER` — the invoker-
rights clause of a procedure, function or package.

## Minimal example

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE run_as_caller
  AUTHID CURRENT_USER
IS
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM staging;
END;
/
```

## ora2pg output (v25.0, `-t PROCEDURE`)

```sql
-- Generated by Ora2Pg, the Oracle database Schema converter, version 25.0
-- Nothing found of type PROCEDURE
```

The procedure is not in the output. At all.

## Observed problem

Of every gap in this registry, the consequence here is the worst: the
object is neither converted with an error nor copied with an "Unsupported"
note — it simply vanishes. And ora2pg's log holds nothing about it: no
warning, not even the DEBUG-level "unhandled line" that appears for, say,
`CREATE CLUSTER`.

**Control measurement.** To confirm that `AUTHID` is the cause rather than
something else in the example, the same procedure was run without the
clause:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE run_as_caller
IS
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM staging;
END;
/
```

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE run_as_caller () AS $body$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM staging;
END;
$body$
LANGUAGE PLPGSQL
;
```

It converts normally. The `AUTHID DEFINER` variant was checked separately —
the same result, `-- Nothing found of type PROCEDURE`.

There will be no error at conversion or at load — the procedure simply
will not be in the target database, and that will be discovered on the
first call from the application. This is the only gap in the registry so
far with `failure_stage = conversion`: the stage was described in
`FAILURE_STAGES` from the moment the taxonomy was introduced and had
stayed empty until now (see `docs/failure-stage-notes.md`).

**Reproducible: YES.** Ora2Pg version: 25.0, PostgreSQL 16.

## Verdict

**Gap confirmed.** Implemented in
`ora2pg_gap_report/detectors/authid_clause.py`. Manual rework: PostgreSQL
does have direct analogues — `AUTHID DEFINER` is `SECURITY DEFINER`, and
`AUTHID CURRENT_USER` is `SECURITY INVOKER` (the default). The clause has
to be removed from the source **before** conversion, or the object will
not appear in the output at all, and the appropriate variant added to the
resulting function.
